clue.text: Bloodsucking insect's low around sierra desert

indicators.note: the word for low wraps itself around the other pieces placed in its middle

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to desert is to quit or abandon

explanation.surface: A description of a blood-drinking bug lying low somewhere in a sierra desert landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra desert' reads as a place, but each word is a separate piece; the 's after 'insect' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito is the familiar biting fly that feeds on blood.

clue.text: Millions beg for protective cover

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
to beg is to ask for something

explanation.surface: Masses of people pleading for some form of shelter or protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A face covering worn for protection, as by a surgeon or welder.

clue.text: Sole broken by hard beach stones

indicators.note: the word for sole is split open so the letter for hard can sit inside it

parts.note: sole means single, the only one
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A shoe sole wrecked by walking over a beach full of hard stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' tempts as the fish or shoe part; here it means only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the loose rounded pebbles that cover many British beaches.

clue.text: Sort of blue extreme Republican in New England state

parts.note: ultra means extreme, as in ultra-conservative

indicators.note: the Republican's letter goes within the name of the state

parts.note: Maine is one of the six New England states
R is the abbreviation for a Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: A political profile: a hard-line Republican living in a New England state, which is a sort of 'blue' area.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultramarine is a deep vivid shade originally made from lapis lazuli.

clue.text: Songbird's quiet after American's finished

indicators.note: the hushing word comes after the American word in the final order

parts.note: thru is the American spelling of through, meaning finished
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A songbird falls silent once the American singer has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a common garden bird known for its singing, such as the song thrush.

clue.text: Four cardinals making the headlines

definitions.meaning: the four cardinal compass points are North, East, West and South
the headlines are the main current reports in the papers or on air

explanation.surface: Four Catholic cardinals doing something scandalous enough to make the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: Current affairs reported in the media; the compass initials N, E, W, S also spell it.

clue.text: Stock English joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A stock or standard English joke, the kind told over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' reads as an adjective for the joke; it is a verb meaning supply.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock or kit out somewhere with supplies is to furnish it.

clue.text: Cheapest way to travel is always poetically in coach

indicators.note: the poetic word for always is placed inside the word for coach

parts.note: a stage, short for stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Travelling by coach is always the cheapest way, as a poet might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship, below decks near the rudder.

clue.text: Son isn't a good man

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A disappointed parent's verdict: the son is not a good man.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy, virtuous person is described as one, so a very good man fits.

clue.text: Strangely put into uncommon ecstasy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed into the word for uncommon

parts.note: rare means uncommon

indicators.note: the letters of put are arranged in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone oddly placed into a rare state of ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is intense joy or delight, a synonym of bliss.

clue.text: Supply a learner driver that's qualified

parts.note: a provision is a supply of something
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: An instruction about providing a car for a learner who has just qualified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Qualified' suggests passing a test; here it means conditional or not final.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualified in the sense of limited or conditional, like a temporary arrangement.

clue.text: Jumper displayed in foie gras shop, perhaps

indicators.note: the answer is on show within the run of clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A sweater on display in a shop selling foie gras, of all places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater; it is a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is famous for its long leaps, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: One who'll stage a play and record it when running

indicators.note: running in the sense of loose or in motion signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stages a play and records it while it runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of the staging and acting of a theatrical production.

clue.text: Where huskies may be used to decorate hat

parts.note: to ice a cake is to decorate it
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Huskies, perhaps the dogs, used to decorate a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sled dogs pull sledges across polar ice sheets such as Greenland's frozen dome.

clue.text: What reduces impact of broadcast carrier

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a bag, as in a carrier bag, carries things

explanation.surface: Something lessening the effect of a broadcasting company's output.
explanation.definitionFit: A car safety cushion inflates in a crash to soften the collision for the occupant.

clue.text: Stab at one by going mad

indicators.note: letters that go mad run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stab at being one, driven by going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab with the blade fixed to a rifle's muzzle is to use it as a verb.

clue.text: Perhaps sexist one when in bed

indicators.note: the pieces for one and when go inside the word bed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone perhaps sexist once they are in bed with you.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexism is one example of prejudice, hence 'perhaps' before the partial definition.

clue.text: Awfully big lie — one fired with yen for fitness

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly arranged and need reshuffling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lit means set on fire
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone sacked for a whopping lie while yearning for fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' turns BIG LIE into ELIGIB; 'fired' means set alight, not sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitability or qualification for something, as in fitness for a role.

clue.text: I had sex appeal to ensnare old fool

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: the word for sex appeal traps the old letter inside it

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A confession: I used my sex appeal to trap an old fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a foolish, stupid person, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Textile worker set up in Surrey docks

indicators.note: set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A textile worker set up in business at Surrey Docks, an area of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unassigned; it is the hiding signal. In a down clue 'set up' turns the letters upward, so the run reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who colours cloth with dyes works in the textile trade.

clue.text: Stumbles around beach regularly twisting muscle

indicators.note: the word for stumbles goes around the other letters

parts.note: trips means stumbles

indicators.note: twisting turns the picked letters round to face the other way
regularly takes every other letter of beach

explanation.surface: Someone tripping on the beach and twisting a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beach' looks like the setting, but only its even letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The large three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: One minding children of girl in New York

indicators.note: the girl's name goes within the abbreviation for New York

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from New York works looking after children.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after a family's young ones, a children's nurse.

clue.text: Church ceremony set down on paper for reading out

indicators.note: reading words out means they are heard, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: to write is to set down on paper

explanation.surface: The order of a church service written down so it can be read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a religious ritual, as in the rites of baptism.

clue.text: One who praises figures I work on some time afterwards

parts.note: to do a job is to work on it
later means at some time afterwards

explanation.surface: An accountant who reckons figures and does the work on them later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' reads as numbers; it means statues or images.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of images or idols, who adores statues as gods.
